title: The World of Metals and Non-metals

learn.hook: The silver vark on a kaju katli is a metal sheet beaten so thin that you can eat it! How can a metal become that thin?
points: Lustre: metals have a shiny surface, especially when freshly cut or polished.
Malleable: metals can be beaten into thin sheets, like aluminium foil and silver vark.
Ductile: metals can be drawn into thin wires, like copper wires.
Sonorous: metals make a ringing sound when struck, which is why bells are made of metal.
Metals are good conductors of heat and electricity. Most are hard, but sodium and potassium are so soft they can be cut with a knife, and mercury is a liquid at room temperature.

example.q: A shopkeeper hammers a lump of material and it spreads into a thin sheet without breaking. Then he taps it and it rings. Is it more likely a metal or a non-metal?
steps: Spreading into a sheet when hammered is called malleability.
Ringing when struck is called sonority.
Both are typical properties of metals.
example.answer: It is most likely a metal.

learn.reallife: A steel tiffin, copper wires in your house, a brass temple bell and aluminium foil around rotis all use special properties of metals.

games.title: Match the property to the example
Metal facts
items: All metals are solids at room temperature.
Mercury is a metal that is liquid at room temperature.
Sodium is soft enough to be cut with a knife.
Sodium and potassium are soft metals. They are stored in kerosene because they react quickly with air and water.
Metals are good conductors of electricity.
That is why wires are made of metals like copper and aluminium.
Ductility means a metal can be drawn into wires.
Copper and aluminium wires are made because these metals are ductile.
Metals break into powder when hammered.
Metals are malleable: they flatten into sheets. Brittle non-metals like sulphur break into powder.

quiz.q: Aluminium can be beaten into thin foil. This property is called:
quiz.explain: Malleability is the ability to be beaten into thin sheets. Ductility is about drawing into wires.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up malleability and ductility

quiz.q: Copper is drawn into thin wires for electric cables. This property is called:
quiz.explain: Ductile metals can be pulled into thin wires without breaking.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up ductility with malleability

quiz.q: Which metal is a liquid at room temperature?
quiz.explain: Mercury is a metal that is liquid at ordinary room temperature. Other common metals are solids.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a soft metal like sodium is liquid

quiz.q: Why are temple and school bells made of metal?
options: Metals are sonorous and ring when struck
quiz.explain: Sonorous materials give a ringing sound when hit, which makes metals ideal for bells.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the word for a ringing property

quiz.q: Which metal is soft enough to be cut with a knife?
quiz.explain: Sodium (and potassium) are soft metals. Most other metals are hard.
quiz.mistake: Believes all metals are hard

quiz.q: A freshly cut piece of metal looks shiny. This shine is called:
quiz.explain: The shiny look of metals is called metallic lustre. Metals can look dull when their surface gets coated by air and moisture over time.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the name of the property

quiz.q: Cooking pans are usually made of metal because metals:
quiz.explain: Metals pass heat quickly from the flame to the food.
quiz.mistake: Confuses conductors and insulators of heat

quiz.q: Which metal is the best conductor of electricity?
quiz.explain: Silver conducts electricity best, with copper a close second. Copper is used more in wires because it is much cheaper.
quiz.mistake: Assumes the most common wire metal (copper) is the best conductor

teach.ask: Gappu found a shiny spoon and a copper wire. What makes metals special? Tell Gappu their properties!
teach.praise: Tweet! Shiny, malleable, ductile, sonorous and good conductors. Gappu knows metals now!
teach.nudge: What happens when you beat a metal with a hammer, or pull it into a wire?

learn.hook: Diamond, the hardest natural substance, and pencil 'lead' are both made of the same non-metal: carbon!
points: Non-metals are usually dull, not sonorous and poor conductors of heat and electricity.
Solid non-metals like sulphur and coal are brittle: they break or turn to powder when hammered.
Many non-metals are gases, such as oxygen, nitrogen, hydrogen and chlorine. Bromine is a liquid non-metal.
Exceptions: iodine is a shiny non-metal, graphite conducts electricity, and diamond is very hard.
When metals burn in air they form oxides that are basic (they turn red litmus blue). Oxides of non-metals like sulphur are acidic (they turn blue litmus red).

example.q: In a teacher's demonstration, a magnesium ribbon burns with a bright white light and leaves white ash. The ash is dissolved in water and tested with litmus. Which litmus changes, and why?
steps: Magnesium is a metal, so its ash is magnesium oxide, a metal oxide.
example.answer: Red litmus turns blue, because magnesium oxide forms a basic solution.

learn.reallife: The oxygen we breathe, the nitrogen that fills chips packets and the chlorine used to clean drinking water are all non-metals.

items.text: The only non-metal that is a liquid at room temperature is ___.
The form of carbon that conducts electricity is ___.
The shiny non-metal used in tincture as an antiseptic is ___.
Oxides of non-metals turn blue litmus ___.

quiz.q: What happens when a lump of sulphur is hammered?
options: It breaks into pieces or powder
quiz.explain: Sulphur is a non-metal, and solid non-metals are brittle.
quiz.mistake: Thinks all solids are malleable like metals

quiz.q: Which non-metal is a liquid at room temperature?
quiz.explain: Bromine is a reddish-brown liquid non-metal. Mercury is also a liquid, but it is a metal.
quiz.mistake: Forgets that mercury is a metal, not a non-metal

quiz.q: Which non-metal is shiny (lustrous)?
quiz.explain: Iodine crystals are shiny, even though iodine is a non-metal.
quiz.mistake: Believes shine always means metal

quiz.q: Sulphur burns to form sulphur dioxide, which dissolves in water. The solution:
quiz.explain: Oxides of non-metals form acidic solutions, and acids turn blue litmus red.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up oxides of metals (basic) and non-metals (acidic)

quiz.q: The oxide formed when magnesium burns gives a solution that is:
quiz.explain: Magnesium is a metal. Metal oxides form basic solutions that turn red litmus blue.
quiz.mistake: Thinks all oxides are acidic

quiz.q: Diamond and graphite are both forms of which element?
quiz.explain: Both are made only of carbon atoms, joined in different ways. That is why they behave so differently.
quiz.mistake: Thinks diamond is a metal because it shines

quiz.q: Which is true for most non-metals?
options: They are poor conductors of heat and electricity
quiz.explain: Most non-metals are dull, brittle (if solid) and poor conductors. Many are gases.
quiz.mistake: Gives non-metals the properties of metals

quiz.q: Which of these is a non-metal gas?
quiz.explain: Nitrogen is a non-metal and makes up most of the air. Sodium, zinc and mercury are metals.
quiz.mistake: Thinks mercury is a gas or a non-metal

teach.ask: Gappu thinks diamond must be a metal because it is shiny and hard. Can you help Gappu understand non-metals?
teach.praise: Chirp chirp! Diamond is carbon, a non-metal with a few surprises. Gappu learned the exceptions too!
teach.nudge: What happens to a non-metal like sulphur when you hammer it?

learn.hook: From the iron in railway tracks to the oxygen cylinders in hospitals, metals and non-metals keep India running!
points: Iron is used for buildings, bridges, railway tracks and machines (mostly as steel).
Copper and aluminium make electric wires; aluminium also makes foil, utensils and aeroplane parts because it is light.
Gold and silver are used in jewellery because they are lustrous and malleable, and gold keeps its shine for a very long time; silver is also beaten into vark for sweets.
Oxygen is needed for breathing; nitrogen is used to make fertilisers and to fill food packets; chlorine is used to clean drinking water.
Carbon (as graphite) is used in pencils, and iodine is used as an antiseptic on wounds.

example.q: Why is the handle of a cooking pan made of wood or plastic, while the pan is made of metal?
steps: The pan must pass heat to the food, so it needs a good conductor: a metal.
The handle must not get hot, so it needs a poor conductor.
Wood and plastic are poor conductors of heat.
example.answer: The metal pan conducts heat to the food; the wooden or plastic handle does not, so it stays safe to hold.

learn.reallife: Look around your kitchen: steel utensils, an aluminium kadhai, a copper-bottom pot and plastic or wooden handles, all chosen for their properties.

games.title: Match the substance to its use

quiz.q: Why is aluminium used to make aeroplane parts?
quiz.explain: Aluminium is a light metal that can be made strong, which suits aeroplanes.
quiz.mistake: Does not connect a use to the right property

quiz.q: Which non-metal is used to make fertilisers?
quiz.explain: Plants need nitrogen to grow. Fertilisers like urea contain nitrogen.
quiz.mistake: Does not know that fertilisers supply nitrogen

quiz.q: Which substance is used to kill germs in drinking water?
quiz.explain: Small amounts of chlorine are added in water treatment plants to kill germs.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up uses of different non-metals

quiz.q: Why are electric wires usually made of copper?
options: Copper is ductile and a good conductor of electricity
quiz.explain: Copper can be drawn into wires (ductile) and carries current well.
quiz.mistake: Forgets that wires need both ductility and good conduction

quiz.q: Silver vark on sweets is possible because silver is:
quiz.explain: Silver can be beaten into extremely thin sheets because it is highly malleable.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up malleable and ductile

quiz.q: Why is gold so popular for jewellery?
options: It is lustrous, malleable and keeps its shine for a long time
quiz.explain: Gold reacts very little with air and water, so it does not lose its shine, and it can be shaped into fine designs.
quiz.mistake: Thinks jewellery metals are chosen for being cheap

quiz.q: Which non-metal is used in pencils?
options: Carbon in the form of graphite
quiz.explain: Despite the name 'pencil lead', the black core is graphite, a form of carbon, mixed with clay.
quiz.mistake: Believes pencils contain the metal lead

quiz.q: Nitrogen is filled in chips packets because:
options: It does not react with food and keeps it fresh
quiz.explain: Nitrogen is unreactive. It keeps oxygen out, so the chips do not go stale quickly and stay protected from crushing.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the gas is there only to cheat on quantity

teach.ask: Gappu wonders why wires are copper but pan handles are plastic. How do we choose a material for a job?
teach.praise: Tweet tweet! Every material is picked for its properties. Gappu is a smart engineer!
teach.nudge: Can you give Gappu one use of a metal and one use of a non-metal?
